nodes.author: askmed01
nodes.text:
1. What is HMPV?

HMPV is a virus that affects the lungs and airways. 

It was discovered in 2001, but it has probably been spreading among humans for a long time. 

It is similar to other viruses like RSV (Respiratory Syncytial Virus) and the flu.

nodes.author: askmed01
nodes.text:
2. Who is at Risk?

HMPV can infect anyone, but some people are more at risk:

• Young children (under 5 years old).

• Older adults (over 65 years old).

• People with weak immune systems, such as those with chronic illnesses or undergoing treatments like chemotherapy.

3. Symptoms of HMPV

The symptoms of HMPV are similar to the flu or a cold and include:

• Fever.
• Runny or stuffy nose.
• Cough and sore throat.
• Trouble breathing or wheezing.
• Feeling tired or weak.

5. How Does HMPV Spread?

HMPV spreads through:

• Respiratory droplets from coughing, sneezing, or talking.

• Direct contact with an infected person.

• Touching surfaces that have the virus and then touching your face.

nodes.author: askmed01
nodes.text:

There is no vaccine or specific treatment for HMPV, but you can reduce your risk by:

7. Treatment

There’s no medicine that directly treats HMPV. Doctors focus on helping you feel better, such as:

• Drinking lots of fluids.

• Taking fever-reducing medicine like ibuprofen.

• Using oxygen therapy if needed in severe cases.
